To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Hungarian language is a clear example of cultural dominance over genetic dominance, and that there was a recent expansion of a Y chromosome marker, 49a,f HT11, in Hungary, probably associated with the spread of the Yamnaya culture.

the Hungarian Palóc and Budapest samples differ from each other and from other European populations in their Y chromosome and mtDNA gene pools, and that the Y chromosome gene pool of both samples is dominated by the proto-European 12f2, the neolithic 49a,f and the paleolithic 49a.f Ht 11.

the Hungarian language could have been an example of cultural, but not genetic, dominance; and that the Hungarian population has a genetic structure similar to that of other European groups, but different from that of other Uralic-speaking groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the low impact of the Magyar invasion on the Hungarian genetic structure, the expansion of 49a,f–YAP−; 12f2 Ht 8Kb–YAP+, the expansion centred on the 49a.f Ht 11, the low frequency of 49a.f–YAP+, 12f2, 50f2 and the high frequency of YAP−; the 49a, f Ht 11 in eastern Europe,
the genetic history of Hungary, but it could also be relevant to the genetic history of Europe and Asia.
the genetic structure of Hungarians and with the origin of the Hungarian language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hungarian gene pool is mainly of paleolithic and neolithic origin, with a very low contribution from the Uralic populations, and a very low contribution also from the Magyars.
the Hungarian gene pool was formed by the interaction between a proto-European and an Asian component, and that it was not affected by the Magyar language.
the Hungarian gene pool is mainly of neolithic and post-neolithic origin and that it has been little affected by Magyars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hungarian gene pool is the result of the mixture of two main components: a paleolithic one and a neolithic one.

the Hungarian gene pool seems to be mainly composed of two different components: the first, the most frequent, is of European origin and is characterized by the presence of YAP−;49a,f Hts 11; 12f2; 50f2−; the second is of Asian origin and is characterized mainly by YAP+ and the absence of 49a,f and 12f2.
the genetic structure of the modern Hungarians is mainly due to a neolithic expansion from the Balkans, with a possible contribution from the Yamnaia expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic structure of Hungarians is very similar to that of other European populations and is mainly the result of the expansion of the neolithic farmers.
the Hungarian language is an example of cultural domination, which is not accompanied by genetic changes in the population.
the Hungarian language was not imposed by a genetic invasion.
